source_documents.title: Hydration-Gated Photoinduced Electron Transfer in BODIPY Dyes

reference_evidence_units.quote: Remarkably, however, fluorescence of 1‐TEG is strongly quenched in water (ΦF = 0.005) (Figure 2b), with faster fluorescence decays and a prominent sub‐nanosecond component
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-TEG
reference_evidence_units.statement: 1-TEG is bright in polar organic solvents and quenched in water with a fast decay component.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Accordingly, ΔG°PET decreases to +0.09 eV in water, rendering charge separation thermodynamically accessible and rationalizing the observed fluorescence quenching.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-TEG
reference_evidence_units.statement: Hydration makes the O-BODIPY core easier to reduce and switches PET on.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The resulting derivative 1‐TEG shows excellent solubility in water, with no signs of aggregation at concentrations of 10− 6–10− 5 M (Figure S2).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-TEG
reference_evidence_units.statement: No aggregation of 1-TEG in water at working concentrations.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: Hydration-gated PET: quenched in water, emissive in MeCN, supported by electrochemistry.
